approved: Farm Household Support (Consequential and Transitional Provisions) Bill 2014

Introduced the companion Farm Household Support (Consequential and Transitional Provisions) Bill, which repeals the redundant Farm Household Support Act 1992 and makes transitional arrangements so recipients can move smoothly onto the new farm household allowance.

Supported the Farm Household Support Bill, noting the farm household allowance provides up to three years of income support from 1 July 2014, replacing the exceptional circumstances relief payment, but criticised the government for abolishing the Standing Committee on Primary Industries and delaying the bill despite months-old drought conditions.

Supported the Farm Household Support Bill, citing national agricultural exports worth $38 billion last year, and outlining the government's $320 million drought package, including $280 million in concessional loans, water infrastructure funding, and mental health services for farming communities.

Said his electorate has been the epicentre of the drought, with the Walgett Shire, which normally produces a million tonnes of wheat, producing none last year, and welcomed the Farm Household Support Bill's $280 million in concessional loans.

Supported the Farm Household Support Bill, said 80 per cent of Queensland's landmass, about 1.5 million square kilometres, is in drought, and criticised the mandatory Horticulture Code of Conduct as unnecessary red tape for Brisbane Markets, a $1 billion-turnover business employing up to 4,000 people, given only 28 inquiries and six mediations occurred under the code in three years.

Detailed the government's drought package, including an interim Farm Household Allowance effective from 3 March, $280 million in concessional loans of up to $1 million or 50 per cent of eligible debt at four per cent for five years, and $10 million for social and mental health support in farming communities.
Disputed the member for Wannon's optimistic outlook for Australian agriculture, arguing no one in the sector would share that confidence, and previewed a rebuttal using ABS statistics.

Supported the Farm Household Support Bill for his 64,000 square kilometre electorate of Barker, cited national agricultural production worth over $47 billion and exports worth about $38 billion last year, and detailed the bill's $2.55 million net farm assets test excluding the family home.

Supported the Farm Household Support Bill, said a John Deere harvester costing $400,000 in the United States costs $800,000 in Australia, and noted Queensland's dairy farmer numbers fell from 2,500 to fewer than 500 in a decade, while the Lockyer Valley alone produces about $250 million in produce annually.

Supported the Farm Household Support Bill, drew on his background modelling Asian demand to argue agriculture faces an opportunity as iron ore prices once did, rising from $20 to $200 a tonne, and said national farm debt climbed from $30 billion to over $70 billion under policy neglect.

Detailed the Farm Household Support Bill, which raises the net farm assets test from $1.5 million to $2.55 million with the family home exempt and allows up to $80,000 in off-farm income, and said 83 families are already accessing the scheme under executive order ahead of its 1 July start.

Announced Labor's bipartisan support for the Farm Household Support (Consequential and Transitional Provisions) Bill, criticised the government's agricultural white paper for omitting climate change and natural resource sustainability from its terms of reference, and cited a report suggesting $500 billion to $600 billion in investment is needed to capitalise on Asian food production opportunities.
